patients.label: 27-year-old unmarried woman with premature ovarian insufficiency, hypothyroidism, Inv(9) and cavernous angioma

identity_evidence.quote: A 27-year-old unmarried female presented with complaints of infrequent cycles only after taking withdrawal treatment for menstruation for the last 11 years.

attribution_limitations: The MRI sentence calls the pontine lesion suggestive of cavernous angioma, while the abstract and conclusion state a solitary or incidentally diagnosed cavernous angioma without hedging.
It is unclear whether "mild pituitary hyperplasia" is also described as suggestive or is a separate MRI finding.
Thyroid function values are given in the hypothyroidism sentence without a stated date, while a later hormonal profile gives a different TSH value; the time of each is not stated.
"for the last 11 years" can attach either to the withdrawal treatment or to the complaint of infrequent cycles; whether the withdrawal treatment is ongoing is not stated.
The neurosurgery advice "to avoid any active intervention and follow-up" is one literal phrase; the source does not say whether follow-up took place.

claims.text: A 27-year-old unmarried woman presented with infrequent cycles that occurred only after taking withdrawal treatment for menstruation for the last 11 years. She had attained menarche at age 14 years with regular 28–30 day cycles for the next 2 years and a non-significant family history. She was diagnosed with hypothyroidism and started on thyroid replacement therapy.
